requirements.quote:
specifically
      SHA-1 which is used in this context with either (1) RSA using
      RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5
requirements.condition: the rsa_pkcs1_sha1 legacy SignatureScheme is used
requirements.forbidden_behavior: bind the scheme to a different hash or RSA signature primitive
requirements.why_checkable: The legacy scheme fixes both the hash and RSA signature primitive.

requirements.quote:
SHA-1 which is used in this context with either (1) RSA using
      RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 or (2) ECDSA.
requirements.condition: the ecdsa_sha1 legacy SignatureScheme is used
requirements.forbidden_behavior: bind the scheme to a different hash or signature primitive
requirements.why_checkable: The legacy scheme fixes both the hash and ECDSA signature primitive.

requirements.quote:
These values refer solely to
      signatures which appear in certificates
requirements.condition: a legacy SHA-1 SignatureScheme value is used
requirements.required_behavior: limit its use to signatures appearing in certificates
requirements.why_checkable: Signature-scheme selection can distinguish certificate signatures from handshake signatures.

requirements.quote:
and
      are not defined for use in signed TLS handshake messages
requirements.condition: a signed TLS handshake message is generated or verified
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use a legacy SHA-1 SignatureScheme for the handshake signature
requirements.why_checkable: CertificateVerify scheme acceptance and generation are directly testable.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints SHOULD NOT negotiate these algorithms but are
      permitted to do so solely for backward compatibility.
requirements.condition: use is not solely required for backward compatibility
requirements.forbidden_behavior: negotiate the legacy SHA-1 signature algorithms
requirements.why_checkable: Negotiated signature algorithms can be observed under normal and explicitly configured compatibility modes.

requirements.quote:
Clients
      offering these values MUST list them as the lowest priority
      (listed after all other algorithms in SignatureSchemeList).
requirements.condition: a client offers legacy SHA-1 SignatureScheme values
requirements.required_behavior: list them after every other algorithm in SignatureSchemeList
requirements.forbidden_behavior: give a legacy SHA-1 value priority over another offered algorithm
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized SignatureSchemeList order can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
TLS 1.3 servers MUST NOT offer a SHA-1 signed certificate unless
      no valid certificate chain can be produced without it
requirements.condition: a TLS 1.3 server can produce a valid certificate chain without a SHA-1-signed certificate
requirements.why_checkable: Certificate-chain selection can be tested with both SHA-1 and non-SHA-1 valid chains available.

requirements.quote:
The signatures on certificates that are self-signed or certificates
   that are trust anchors are not validated
requirements.condition: a self-signed certificate begins the certification path
requirements.required_behavior: do not validate that certificate's self-signature as part of path validation
requirements.why_checkable: Certificate-path validation behavior can be exercised with a self-signed path origin.

requirements.quote:
The signatures on certificates that are self-signed or certificates
   that are trust anchors are not validated
requirements.condition: a trust-anchor certificate begins the certification path
requirements.required_behavior: do not validate the trust anchor's certificate signature as part of path validation
requirements.why_checkable: Certificate-path validation can distinguish trust-anchor handling from subordinate-certificate validation.

requirements.quote:
TLS 1.3
   implementations willing to negotiate TLS 1.2 MUST behave in
   accordance with the requirements of [RFC5246] when negotiating that
   version.
requirements.required_behavior: behave according to the applicable RFC 5246 requirements
requirements.why_checkable: The local evidence delegates the constrained behavior to another document and is not self-contained enough for a concrete check.

requirements.quote:
They MUST NOT be offered or negotiated by any
      implementation.
requirements.condition: an implementation constructs a signature algorithm offer
requirements.forbidden_behavior: offer an unallocated legacy TLS 1.2 hash/signature pair
requirements.why_checkable: Generated signature algorithm lists can be checked for the prohibited legacy pairs.

requirements.quote:
They MUST NOT be offered or negotiated by any
      implementation.
requirements.condition: an implementation selects a signature algorithm
requirements.forbidden_behavior: negotiate an unallocated legacy TLS 1.2 hash/signature pair
requirements.why_checkable: Negotiated signature scheme selection can be exercised with prohibited legacy pairs.

requirements.quote:
In particular, MD5 [SLOTH], SHA-224, and DSA
      MUST NOT be used.
requirements.condition: an implementation generates or verifies a TLS signature
requirements.why_checkable: Signature algorithm dispatch can be inspected and tested for MD5 rejection.

requirements.quote:
In particular, MD5 [SLOTH], SHA-224, and DSA
      MUST NOT be used.
requirements.condition: an implementation generates or verifies a TLS signature
requirements.why_checkable: Signature algorithm dispatch can be inspected and tested for SHA-224 rejection.

requirements.quote:
In particular, MD5 [SLOTH], SHA-224, and DSA
      MUST NOT be used.
requirements.condition: an implementation generates or verifies a TLS signature
requirements.why_checkable: Signature algorithm dispatch can be inspected and tested for DSA rejection.

requirements.quote:
If TLS 1.2 is negotiated, implementations MUST be prepared
      to accept a signature that uses any curve that they advertised in
      the "supported_groups" extension.
requirements.condition: TLS 1.2 is negotiated and an ECDSA signature uses a curve advertised in supported_groups
requirements.required_behavior: accept the signing curve regardless of the TLS 1.3 curve-specific SignatureScheme semantics
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reject it solely because the SignatureScheme name identifies another curve
requirements.why_checkable: TLS 1.2 signatures can be generated over each advertised curve and acceptance observed.

requirements.quote:
Implementations that advertise support for RSASSA-PSS (which is
      mandatory in TLS 1.3) MUST be prepared to accept a signature using
      that scheme even when TLS 1.2 is negotiated.
requirements.condition: an implementation advertises RSASSA-PSS and negotiates TLS 1.2
requirements.required_behavior: accept a signature using the advertised RSASSA-PSS scheme
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reject the signature solely because TLS 1.2 was negotiated
requirements.why_checkable: A TLS 1.2 handshake can use an advertised RSASSA-PSS signature and exercise verification.

requirements.quote:
In TLS 1.2,
      RSASSA-PSS is used with RSA cipher suites.
requirements.required_behavior: use it with an RSA cipher suite
requirements.forbidden_behavior: bind it to a non-RSA cipher suite
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated cipher suite and signature scheme are both observable handshake state.
